subject: Energy
title: Energy Efficiency Standards
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Energy Efficiency Standards.

hook.text: Efficiency standards set minimum performance rules—forcing appliances, vehicles, and buildings to waste less energy.

buildup.text: US fuel economy standards (CAFE) have saved billions of barrels of oil since 1975—gradually raising the MPG floor.

discovery.text: Building codes requiring insulation, efficient windows, and heat pumps cut heating demand by 50–80%.

twist.text: Appliance standards are invisible heroes—efficient fridges, washers, and ACs save more energy than many solar farms.

climax.text: The IEA calls efficiency the 'first fuel'—the cheapest and fastest way to reduce energy demand and emissions.

punchline.text: Use less energy for the same result—efficiency is invisible power.

quiz.question: Why does the IEA call efficiency the 'first fuel'?
options: It's the cheapest and fastest way to cut demand
